title: 15s upbeat retail pulse
prompt: A 15-second upbeat retail pulse in E major at 128 BPM, written to sit under a direct-to-consumer ad voiceover. It opens on a bright chord-stab hit at frame 0 (kick, crash and a full E major stab). It then settles into a four-on-the-floor groove: off-beat bass, syncopated chord plucks moving I-V-vi-IV, claps on 2 and 4, and shimmering hats. A filtered noise riser and a snare roll build through bar 5. The bar at 9.375 s (the "about 10 s" lift) adds a crash, a wide pad and a sparkling sixteenth-note arpeggio. The groove then drops out for half a beat, a reverse swell pulls in, and a clean button tag on the tonic lands exactly on frame 420 (14.0 s) and rings out to silence. Everything below 120 Hz is reserved for a mono kick and bass. The music bus is gently scooped around 2.5 kHz so a voice sits on top.
notes:
Kick and off-beat bass are the only content below 120 Hz (mono, side channel high-passed at 120 Hz); plucks, pad and arp are additive and band-limited (no aliasing), sidechain-pumped from the kick, and scooped -2.5 dB at 2.5 kHz to leave a voiceover pocket.
Arc: frame-0 tonic stab + crash, sparse filtered intro bar, full groove from bar 2 (I-V-vi-IV), SVF noise riser + snare roll through bar 5, lift on the bar-6 downbeat (9.375 s) with crash, octave-doubled bright plucks, wide pad and 16th arpeggio, then a half-beat drop-out with reverse swell and a V-I button tag exactly on frame 420.
Mastered with a 4x-oversampled look-ahead gain limiter (~2 dB GR, no clipping) iterated to -14 LUFS / -1.3 dBTP, TPDF-dithered to 16-bit.
